findings.summary: approval_state_of never checks model.spec_slug against the filename slug
findings.suggestion: After load(), treat the approval as invalid when model.spec_slug != slug.

reasoning.observe: approval_state_of checks only approval.content_hash vs approval_content_hash(model).
reasoning.trace: Every land entry and the autopilot gate funnel through it with the filename slug.
reasoning.infer: An approved SPEC-Y copied verbatim to SPEC-X passes the hash check.
reasoning.conclude: An unreviewed SPEC reads approved under another name (copy-as-template path).

findings.summary: approve() is an unlocked read-modify-write racing mark_tested/mark_judged
findings.suggestion: Serialize load/mutate/write on the machine SPEC.

findings.summary: Approval probe's git worktree add/remove runs inside the merge fence, exceeding its documented timeout budget
findings.suggestion: Move the detached-checkout probe outside the merge fence.

reasoning.observe: _branch_approval_holds runs inside _acquire_merge_fence when the worktree dir is gone.
reasoning.trace: _FENCE_TIMEOUT is sized for the stash + merge worst case only.
reasoning.infer: Two more 60s-capped git calls push worst-case hold past the waiter budget.
reasoning.conclude: A concurrent land can spuriously time out on the fence.

findings.summary: The config-redirection fix still permits a worktree-off bypass. Changing harness.yaml's spec.dir from specs/ to elsewhere/ makes both directory lookups use elsewhere/. An invalid or unapproved SPEC remaining under specs/ is then invisible to wrapup_land, even when its slug is supplied. Preserve the prior configured location from git as well as the current location when discovering files.
findings.evidence: _spec_dirs reads both directories from the current filesystem. With base == checkout and spec.dir changed to elsewhere/, a changed specs/SPEC-demo.machine.yaml is omitted and the explicit demo slug returns no_spec/ok.

findings.summary: The first matching directory can mask a changed SPEC in the other directory. If a branch changes spec.dir to new-specs/ and retains an approved same-slug copy under specs/, discovery reduces the changed path to its slug and approval_state reads only the old copy. The unapproved new SPEC can land through task-land or finalize. Keep discovered file identities and check every relevant file instead of collapsing them to a first-match slug.
findings.evidence: An in-memory probe with an approved specs/SPEC-demo.machine.yaml and an unapproved new-specs/SPEC-demo.machine.yaml returned only demo: approved/ok, despite git reporting the new-specs file as changed.

findings.summary: Normalize configured directories before matching git paths. A valid spec.dir of ./specs/ produces the prefix ./specs/SPEC-, while git emits specs/SPEC-.... Consequently, loop finalize discovers no SPECs and lands even an invalid approval. Named-slug checks can conceal this defect in task-land tests, but finalize supplies no slugs.
findings.evidence: With _spec_dirs returning ['./specs/'] and git reporting specs/SPEC-demo.machine.yaml, land_states(base, checkout) returned [].
